items.title: 13.1 Volatility of chlorine, bromine and iodine

source_refs.note: Topic 13.1 with the Interesting Information box on bromine, printed page 293.

blocks.text: Chlorine being a liquid is very volatile at room temperature and disperses quickly in the air. Bromine, a liquid, is less volatile than chlorine but more volatile than iodine; it evaporates readily, releasing toxic fumes at room temperature, with an orange vapour and a strong, unpleasant smell (its name comes from the Greek 'bromos', stench). Iodine is the least volatile of the three: at room temperature its solid state shows lower volatility than chlorine and bromine. Volatility therefore decreases from chlorine to iodine, because of the increasing molecular mass, the larger outer shell and the stronger intermolecular (London dispersion) forces down the group.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book calls chlorine a liquid. At room temperature chlorine is a gas (bromine is the liquid and iodine a solid), which is why it is the most volatile of the three.
Why is chlorine more volatile than bromine and iodine?
